clue.text: Rally about finished in outskirts of Coventry

parts.note: re is a preposition meaning about or concerning

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, the containment that 'in' signals here
the outskirts of a place are its edges, so take the outer letters of the word

parts.note: something finished is over

explanation.surface: A motorsport rally rounds off on the edge of Coventry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' takes C and Y from Coventry, and 'in' puts OVER between them to make COVERY after RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rally in prices or health is a recovery, a bounce back after a fall.

clue.text: Based in Paris is blushing about it

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: someone blushing goes red
est is French for is

explanation.surface: Someone stationed in Paris turns red over something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts EST, the French word for 'is', inside RED; 'it' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Rested means lay or was supported on something, as a weight is based on a foundation.

clue.text: Pick fellows to leave church office

indicators.note: to leave means to go away from the word, so those letters are dropped from it

parts.note: F is fellow, so FF is fellows

explanation.surface: Fellows quit a church office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' takes FF out of OFFICE, leaving OICE after CH.
explanation.definitionFit: A choice is a pick, the one selected from the options.

clue.text: Clergyman is against taking one vehicle

parts.note: V for versus, meaning against
I is the Roman numeral one
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A priest objects to sharing his car.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a parish priest in the Church of England.

clue.text: Measure way in for thief

indicators.note: the way goes in the measure, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a ruler is a measuring stick
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Checking the size of a route for a burglar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ST inside RULER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler is a thief who steals cattle or horses.

clue.text: Animal found wandering in Rome

indicators.note: letters that wander roam from their places, so the fodder words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some creature has been spotted roaming the streets of Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges the six letters of IN ROME.
explanation.definitionFit: A merino is a breed of sheep prized for its fine wool.

clue.text: Traded with journalist, taking ten coins

indicators.note: taking means holding in, so the journalist wraps the rest

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
X is the Roman numeral ten
loose coins are change

explanation.surface: A reporter does a deal, pocketing ten coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' puts X and CHANGE inside ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have exchanged goods is to have traded or swapped them.

clue.text: Oddly it purred when entered suddenly!

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters fall into a strange order

explanation.surface: The cat purred strangely when someone burst in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' rearranges IT PURRED; it does not take odd letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to burst or rush in violently, so irrupted means broke in suddenly.

clue.text: Threatening to get extra performers

parts.note: over means extra, left over
the cast is the performers in a show

explanation.surface: A theatre threatens to hire more actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Threatening' describes a sky that threatens rain.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcast sky is dark with cloud, looking as if rain will come.

clue.text: Display by patient exhibitor

parts.note: to display something is to show it
a doctor's patient is a case

explanation.surface: A doctor puts a patient on display like an exhibit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Display' looks like the definition, but it supplies SHOW; the definition is 'exhibitor', a glass cabinet that exhibits things.
explanation.definitionFit: A showcase is a glass cabinet in which items are put on view, so it is a thing that exhibits.

clue.text: Rare cars repaired by engineer

indicators.note: repaired cars are put back together, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

parts.note: CE stands for civil engineer

explanation.surface: Unusual motors get fixed by a mechanic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' rearranges CARS to SCAR, and CE (civil engineer) follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce is in short supply, hard to come by.

clue.text: Fish — the angler's first thought!

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An angler's first thought is fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or notion.

clue.text: Stop and ring in, as surrounded

indicators.note: the ring is put in the stop, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a stop is an end
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A police instruction to halt and call in, with suspects surrounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts CIRCLE inside END, between EN and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Encircled means ringed round on every side, enclosed.

clue.text: Wasp I caught in something savoury

indicators.note: the answer lies in the letters of the clue's own words running across them

explanation.surface: A wasp has been trapped in a savoury jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across WASP I CAUGHT, taking ASP from Wasp, I and the C of caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a clear meat jelly used to set savoury dishes.

clue.text: Shoulder uncovered, say

indicators.note: say signals that a word is spoken, so the spelling changes but the sound stays

parts.note: uncovered means bare, naked

explanation.surface: Someone has a bare shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoulder' is a verb here, to carry a burden; BARE sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder a load or responsibility is to bear it, carry its weight.

clue.text: Telling to bring about five in, in other words

parts.note: to effect is to bring about

indicators.note: the five goes in the abbreviation, one piece inside the other

parts.note: IE stands for id est, that is, in other words
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: An instruction to bring about five changes, phrased differently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts V inside IE to make IVE after EFFECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A telling argument is an effective one, striking and persuasive.

clue.text: A port and lager is ordered

indicators.note: ordered can mean put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: In a bar, someone orders a port and a lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges LAGER and IS into the Algerian capital; 'port' is a harbour city, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Algiers is the capital of Algeria and a major Mediterranean harbour city.

clue.text: Wood with many a pig in

indicators.note: a pig goes in the word many, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
a hog is a pig

explanation.surface: A wood with lots of pigs in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A HOG inside MANY, between M and ANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahogany is a hard reddish-brown timber used in fine furniture.

clue.text: Prospect of more cuts, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps means maybe in another form, so the letters may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A worried employee eyes the possibility of further cutbacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges MORE CUTS; 'Prospect' is a person, a possible buyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect in sales is a potential client, someone who may buy.

clue.text: Left without fuel Iraq turned to water supplier

indicators.note: turned means twisted round into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
without means lacking, so one letter is dropped from the word beside it

explanation.surface: Short of fuel, Iraq switches to a water supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops L from FUEL to give FUE, and 'turned' rearranges FUE with IRAQ.
explanation.definitionFit: An aquifer is a layer of porous rock holding groundwater that wells draw on.

clue.text: Bank charge raised after year end

indicators.note: after says the raised piece follows the other
the end of a word is its last letter
raised means lifted up, and in a down clue the word reads upwards

parts.note: a fee is a charge

explanation.surface: A bank puts up its charges after the year end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns FEE to EEF, and 'after' puts it after R, the end of 'year'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge of rock or sand near the surface of the sea, a bank.

clue.text: They swim to English rules

parts.note: cod are fish, things that swim

explanation.surface: A rallying call for English swimmers to obey the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They swim' points to fish in general; COD is one kind, plural as well as singular.
explanation.definitionFit: A code is a set of rules, as in a highway or dress code.

clue.text: Create concoction right for food supplier

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the word's letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A cook concocts something for the food stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction' rearranges CREATE, and R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer provides food and drink for events.

clue.text: Redhead puts up with love in dazed state!

indicators.note: up means upwards, and in a down clue the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
the head of the word red is its first letter, R

explanation.surface: A redhead gets lovestruck and dazed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PUTS to STUP; O and R follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a state of near-unconsciousness, as from drink or shock.

clue.text: Forces members into painting

annotationWithheld.why: Forces members into painting (6): FORCES rearranged gives FRESCO, but neither 'members' nor 'into' works as an anagram signal and no container parse uses both; the clue as held looks misread and no source found

clue.text: A new topic of vision

indicators.note: a new version of the word is a rearranged one, a fresh order of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone raises a fresh subject about eyesight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges TOPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is an adjective meaning relating to the eye or sight.

clue.text: Sort of fan once used on farm vehicle

parts.note: ex means former, once
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: A fan who was once a devotee of tractors on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fan' suggests a devotee, but it is a ventilating device.
explanation.definitionFit: An extractor fan draws stale air or steam out of a kitchen or bathroom.

clue.text: Now insult half, being sexually explicit

parts.note: AD, anno domini, is the present era, now

indicators.note: half takes one half of the word, here the back half

explanation.surface: An insult deliberately crude in tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes ULT, the second half of insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Adult used of films or books means containing explicit sexual material.

clue.text: Part of body of tramp I knocked over

indicators.note: something knocked over is jumbled, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to knocking down a tramp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' rearranges TRAMP and I; it is not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: The armpit is the hollow under the shoulder where the arm joins the body.

clue.text: Is unusually prim, thus wins

indicators.note: unusually means in an unusual way, so the letters take an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone untypically prudish therefore comes out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges PRIM and THUS; 'Is' at the front joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumphs are victories, so the plural noun matches wins.

clue.text: See Elizabeth for special delivery

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, and York is an archbishop's see
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A notice to go and see the Queen for a special delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' is a cricket ball bowled; a yorker is aimed to land at the batsman's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a yorker is a hard-to-play ball pitched right at the batsman's toes.

clue.text: Speaker: I love religious music!

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A preacher declares a love of sacred music.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is nil in tennis scores, shown as O.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large choral work on a sacred theme, such as Handel's Messiah.
